what_it_does: Ion-trap quantum computers hold individual charged atoms (ions) in place using electric fields and manipulate them with lasers to perform quantum computations. To run a multi-qubit circuit, ions must sometimes be physically moved — shuttled — to bring distant pairs close enough to interact, and each shuttle step introduces errors and time delay. BOSS is a scheduling algorithm that groups nearby quantum operations into blocks so that the ions needed for one block are already positioned correctly for the next, minimizing the total number of shuttle moves required across a circuit with thousands of operations. The paper tests the approach on realistic hardware parameters including sympathetic cooling (using a second species of ion to shed heat and restore qubit quality). This is from the abstract only.
